units.text: EXT. FLOODED RICE PADDY - DAWN
Mist hangs low over water the color of tin.
A broken irrigation sluice stands like a gallows in the middle distance.
Four soldiers crouch behind a mud dike, helmets slick with rain.
SERGEANT WALTER "BUCK" DOYLE (40s, square jaw, a face carved for recruiting posters) scans the treeline through field glasses.
CORPORAL RAFAEL ORTEGA (20s, radio on his back, quick to smile) fiddles with a dial.
PRIVATE EZRA FINCH (19, freckled, rifle held too tightly) shivers beside him.
LIEUTENANT HIROSHI TANAKA (30s, Nisei interpreter, spectacles taped at the hinge) kneels apart, a map folded in his gloved hands.
Quiet, all of you.
units.name: DOYLE

units.text: I'm just saying, Sarge, the set's dead. Nothing but static.
units.name: ORTEGA

units.text: Maybe they're jamming it.
units.name: FINCH

units.text: They aren't. The transmitter's been underwater since the rains.
units.name: TANAKA

units.text: I said quiet.
units.name: DOYLE

units.text: Sarge, I think I saw something move.
units.name: FINCH

units.text: Where?
units.name: ORTEGA

units.text: Left of the sluice. Don't point.
units.name: TANAKA

units.text: Finch, stay down. Ortega, forget the radio. Lieutenant, how far to the ridge?
units.name: DOYLE

units.text: Two kilometers across open water.
units.name: TANAKA

units.text: Open water. Swell.
units.name: ORTEGA

units.text: I can't swim so good.
units.name: FINCH

units.text: You can wade.
units.name: DOYLE

units.text: Across the paddy, a rooster crows.
Everyone freezes.
Then, from the treeline, a woman's voice calls out in a tongue none of them knows.
She says to come in. She says it is safe.
units.name: TANAKA

units.text: Do you believe her?
units.name: DOYLE

units.text: No.
units.name: TANAKA

units.text: Then why are you smiling?
units.name: ORTEGA

units.text: Because she said it twice.
units.name: TANAKA

units.text: A mortar whistles.
All four dive into the mud as the sluice erupts in white water.
Move! Move!
units.name: DOYLE

units.text: They scramble along the dike, bent double, Finch last, dragging his rifle through the muck.
